title: fix(staging): export COCO boxes in screen coordinates
body: ## Summary Compute COCO bounding boxes from the bounds of all source vertices in screen coordinates. The current exporter assumes a particular ordering of the first three points and treats every coordinate system as having a top-left origin. This can move a valid rectangle, give a zero height to clockwise vertices, or export Cartesian coordinates on the wrong side of the page. Use the existing coordinate-system conversion to a `PixelSpace` of the same dimensions, then calculate the minimum corner, width, and height. Reuse those dimensions for the existing bounding-box area. Missing coordinates retain their empty-box/`None`-area representation, and source metadata is unchanged. ## Validation - Added 13 regression cases; unchanged upstream produces 11 failures and 2 passes. - Cover four vertex orders in PixelSpace and PointSpace, triangle and diamond bounds, opposite corners, missing coordinates, and source metadata preservation. - A native `pycocotools.mask.iou` calculation confirms unit overlap with the independently specified screen-space rectangle. - New tests plus the existing COCO export and coordinate-system module: **30 passed** on Python 3.12. The full repository suite was not run. - Lockfile-pinned Ruff 0.15.10 check/format and `git diff --check` passed. ## Checklist - [x] The PR title is a user-facing release-note entry with a conventional commit prefix. - [ ] Please apply the `bug` category label during maintainer triage. - [x] No changelog edit or version bump; this restores the COCO bounding-box convention.
